item.title: Army Reserve patient insertion team amplifies readiness, interoperability during UC26
item.description:
SCOTT AIR FORCE BASE, Ill. — More than 30 Army Reserve Soldiers of the Aurora, Colorado-based 7450th Medical Operational Readiness Unit, a downtrace unit of the Army Reserve Medical Command hierarchy, trained and operated as the patient insertion team in synchronization with other military and civilian personnel during Exercise Ultimate Caduceus 2026, henceforth known as UC26, here Sept. 7-12, 2026.
UC26 is a U.S. Transportation Command-led annual patient movement field training exercise held here, Alpena, Michigan; Boise, Idaho and Fort Campbell, Kentucky. Approximately 400 military and civilian personnel from AR-MEDCOM downtrace units, USTRANSCOM, U.S. Northern Command, U.S. Strategic Command, U.S. Air Force aeromedical evacuation crews, Critical Care Air Transport Teams, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, Defense Health Agency, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and myriad commercial partners all coordinated with each other in the shared responsibility in ensuring unity of effort.

item.title: Alaska, Kosovo youth build friendships through pen pal program
item.description:
Future School Director Festa Shabani still vividly remembers the arrival of U.S. Soldiers following the Kosovo War in 1999. Determined that future generations understand that history and the enduring friendship between the United States and Kosovo, she has spent years building relationships with Soldiers serving in the Kosovo Force.
This spring, that partnership inspired an international pen pal program connecting children in the Alaska Army National Guard Child and Youth Program with students at Future School in Gjilan, Kosovo.

item.title: 188th ISR Group Connects Three Locations During Tactical Exercise
item.description: The 188th Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Group demonstrated its ability to rapidly establish reliable, interoperable communications during a multi-location tactical exercise across Arkansas. Working alongside the 189th and 19th Airlift Wings, the team deployed the Radio Interoperability System to connect cellular, VHF and UHF networks, supporting command and control operations for C-130H aircraft and ground forces. The exercise marked a first-of-its-kind test of the 188th Wing’s RIOS system and provided valuable lessons for future communications deployments in austere and dynamic environments.
